clauses.title: CL-D104 records that /tidd-pr runs through the packaged driver
clauses.section: ## CL-D104 — /tidd-pr runs through the packaged driver
requires: tetsuh/pi-tidd-agents#224
The parent judges an outcome by the lines the driver prints, never by its exit status
running its command again after completion is not a retry
This narrows CL-D19 and Mode dispatch, which read exactly one mode reference after mode parsing, to the prose path.
The Skill's other sections, the shared references and the mode references stay as they are, as the specification the driver and the gates implement (D2)
they measured 156,472 bytes on this change, so the ceiling rises to 162,000 bytes on the CL-D43 terms, leaving 5,528 bytes
Letting the parent compose or change a request the driver builds, judge an outcome by exit status, or interrupt a running gate, or removing the dispatch section, requires a new owner decision.

clauses.title: The Skill's dispatch section
requires: a pull request of the repository of the current checkout runs through the packaged driver, which sequences the round, not you
run `node <skill-dir>/driver/<driver>.js start --pr <number> --repo <owner/name>`
If the call is refused or returns no run id, report it and stop; never change the object.
Otherwise wait for the runner's own completion of that run; never interrupt, pause, steer, or cancel it.
When a line begins `WAIT:`, the run has not completed

4. When the last line the driver prints begins `PROSE_PATH:` (a note your shell tool adds after it, such as the exit code, is not the driver's), continue with Mode dispatch below in the parsed mode, whatever reference that line names.
6. Otherwise, when a driver command prints none of these lines, report the last 30 lines of its combined output and stop; never retry or continue by hand.

Add `--language-profile "conversation=<language>; github.issue=<language>; github.pull_request=<language>; external_sites=<sites>"` with the profile CL-D16 resolved for this run (`<sites>` is `{}` when it names none)
(a note your shell tool adds after it, such as the exit code, is not the driver's)

only when you start the driver directly (`/tidd-pr` never passes it)

clauses.title: The driver prints the send-back line itself
requires: function sendBack(message) { process.stdout.write(`PROSE_PATH: ${String(message).split(/[\x00-\x1f\x7f-\x9f\u2028\u2029]+/).join(' ')}\n`); process.exit(2); }

clauses.title: The section, its command sequence, the record and the raise are pinned
requires: Issue #224 the Skill sends the round to the packaged driver before any mode reference is read
Issue #224 the dispatch section\'s command sequence runs one review-only round to a terminal outcome
Issue #224 the contract records the dispatch and README names the one way to run a round
Issue #224 CL-D104 raises the authority ceiling once, with the headroom asserted at the raise
Issue #224 a review-only diff that is not UTF-8 ends on a PROSE_PATH line after FINISHED
Issue #224 a head that is not local is sent back on a PROSE_PATH line
Issue #224 a send-back without a base .tidd.json carries no git error output
Issue #224 a send-back carries no git warning either
Issue #224 a send-back naming a checkout path with a line break is still one PROSE_PATH line
Issue #224 a stop reason holding a Unicode line separator cannot forge a PROSE_PATH last line
Issue #224 a NEXT line holding a Unicode line separator stays one line with its value unchanged
